approach: Docs-only change. Create docs/design/context-engineer.md (about 400 lines, no code) with sections: purpose and mapping, what exists today, part 1 conventions table (convention, measure, threshold, enforcement or prose-only), part 2 inputs and post-mortem, cadence, budgets, restructuring queue, relations, alternatives, build plan. Append D130 (proposed) to docs/decisions.md in the D129 format, add one CHANGELOG line under Unreleased/Changed, and add a short cross-reference to section 8 of docs/design/hestia.md. Every figure cites its source or is labeled an estimate. Parts of the design that depend on unbuilt things are marked as unbuilt.

decisions.choice: Confirm Hermes (context and handoffs) as the owner of the craft, with Hestia as a consumer and keeper of knowledge. Hestia's sweep carries the recurring checks; Hermes sets conventions and runs the post-mortem.
decisions.reason: BRIEF.md pantheon row (line 597) gives Hermes 'context, handoffs'; line 912 says structured handoffs. hestia.md section 8 and D127 give Hestia knowledge, docs and tidiness, and say she does not gate. Splitting by craft (set rules and what agents read) versus upkeep (sweep for drift) matches both rows. The ontology.toml entry warns Hermes the god and Hermes Agent are two things; the doc says it means the pantheon role.

rejected.why: hestia.md is already ten jobs and a sweep, not a craft owner; D127 keeps her out of gating.
No evidence needs it; Hermes's row already covers context and handoffs.
Part 1 (file size, doc shape) is what makes part 2 cheap; splitting the craft loses the link.

decisions.choice: Each convention gets a measure, a threshold labeled as estimate, and an enforcement line: 'mechanism: <named measure>' or 'prose-only'. Measures that depend on unbuilt checks (code-health 5p65, Jev zc0v) are written as 'needs X, not built'.
decisions.reason: The 'mechanism' default and criterion 4 forbid assuming unbuilt things exist. A grep of docs/ finds no file naming the introspector, the requirements engineer, 5p65 or zc0v, so the doc must say these are request-only and state the interface it assumes.

rejected.option: Assume the code-health check exists and specify its output
rejected.why: Not in the snapshot; would invent facts.
Criterion 1 requires a threshold; label them estimates and set a calibration step in job 1.

decisions.choice: Post-mortem is a small recorded step after each failed, rejected or planning-stopped job: one question ('what context would have prevented this?'), answer classified into a fixed set of changes (add a system-facts line, add a failure class, edit brief assembly, vocabulary term, spec fix, none), with a cap on prompt-budget growth (each addition must name what it displaces when the set is over 95% of budget).
decisions.reason: Grounds part 2 in evidence: planning stops from unstated facts, 7 retries lost earlier verifier findings, reader at 1997 of 2000 (system-facts budget lines). The budget makes additions trade-offs rather than growth.

rejected.why: Grows unbounded and is not read; contradicts one-fact-in-one-place.
Request includes rejected and planning-stopped jobs.

decisions.choice: Restructuring is queued as ordinary requests, never edited by the role. Hermes files them with the measure that slipped; a cap on open restructure requests (estimate 3) and a rule that a split must be behavior-preserving with the old test suite unchanged.
decisions.reason: Matches hestia.md's rule that fixes go through the pipeline and D127's non-gating stance. Splitting gh.rs and produce_and_verify is out of scope now; the doc only names them as first queue candidates.

rejected.option: Block jobs that touch oversized files
rejected.why: Gating belongs to Artemis; would stall urgent work.

decisions.choice: Cite evidence by source: gh.rs 5,276 lines, produce_and_verify 724 lines, decision log 3,231 lines, 7 retries, reader 1997 of 2000. The producer must re-measure each (wc -l via file read, grep counts) and, where a figure cannot be re-measured from the snapshot (7 retries, planning stops, which need records/), label it 'stated by the request, not measured here'.
decisions.reason: Evidence default; the snapshot has no records/. The decisions.md file is now longer than 3,231 lines (D129 ends near 3262), so the doc must state the count at the base commit and note the request's figure.

decisions.choice: Build plan of about six jobs, each one producer run, with behavior acceptance bullets: (1) measure tool for size conventions as a test-visible report on a fixture with a known oversize file, (2) docs question-to-file map plus index check that fails on an unindexed doc, (3) decision log split plan/archive with a link checker, (4) post-mortem record and brief-assembly change that carries the earlier verifier findings into retries, (5) budget guard that fails when a set exceeds 95% unless an offset is named, (6) restructure-queue filer with cap.
decisions.reason: Criterion 6. Each bullet names a failing case first (fixture or removed fix) then the pass, per the behavior-evidence default.

rejected.why: Out of scope; job 3 only designs the archive move as a later request.

files.purpose: The design: mapping, conventions with measures, part 2 and post-mortem, cadence, budgets, restructure queue, relations, alternatives, build plan.
Append D130 (proposed) after D129 in the same format; do not edit other entries.
One line under [Unreleased] / Changed naming the design and D130; design only.
Add a short cross-reference in section 8: the context engineer role sets the conventions Hestia's docs checks measure; changes nothing else.

steps: Read BRIEF.md lines 590-610 and 905-915, hestia.md in full, requirements-map.md header, scope-guard.md section on roles, and ontology.toml Hermes entry; note what each says.
Measure at the base: line counts of crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs, the produce_and_verify function span, docs/decisions.md; read the budget lines in system-facts. Record the figures with sources.

Draft context-engineer.md: question-to-file map at top; sections 1 Mapping (confirmed, reason); 2 What exists today (table with sources, unbuilt marked); 3 Part 1 conventions table (convention, measure, threshold estimate, mechanism or prose-only); 4 Part 2 inputs and post-mortem (triggers, question, outcome classes, budget-displacement rule); 5 Measures and cadence; 6 Budgets; 7 Restructuring queue and cap; 8 Relations to Hestia, code-health check, Jev checks, introspector, requirements engineer; 9 Alternatives; 10 Build plan of about six jobs with behavior acceptance bullets (failing case first); 11 Not measured.
Append D130 to docs/decisions.md after D129 in the same bullet format, status proposed, with provenance.
Add the CHANGELOG line under [Unreleased] Changed.
Add the cross-reference to hestia.md section 8.
Run cargo test --locked (policy scans, budget test) and git diff --stat to confirm only the four doc files changed.

risks.risk: The doc invents facts about unbuilt checks, the introspector or the requirements engineer.
risks.mitigation: A 'what exists today' table lists each with its source file or 'request only'; all dependent measures say 'needs X'.

risks.risk: The doc itself is long and breaks its own conventions.
risks.mitigation: Keep it under about 450 lines with a question-to-file map at the top and each fact stated once; apply the part 1 thresholds to itself.

risks.risk: The decisions.md edit lands inside another entry, as in D128's case.
risks.mitigation: Append at end of file after D129 only; the producer checks the heading order after editing.
Do not write any personal address or run-location words; run cargo test --locked to confirm.

risks.risk: Numbers drift from the base files.
risks.mitigation: Re-measure line counts with Read/Grep count at the base and state the base-commit figure beside the request's figure.

demonstrations.method: Read the finished doc and check each named convention appears with a measure, threshold and enforcement label; spot-check one threshold against a measured file.
demonstrations.observes: docs/design/context-engineer.md is added; reading the part 1 table shows rows for file size, function size, one concern per module, one fact in one place, question-to-file map and index, each with measure, threshold and 'mechanism' or 'prose-only'.
demonstrations.fails_without: A convention row lacking a measure, threshold or enforcement label is a defect found on reading the table.

demonstrations.method: Read the part 2 section for the inputs (briefs, system-facts, failure classes, vocabulary, spec) and the post-mortem step with its trigger set and outcome classes.
demonstrations.observes: The section names the three triggers (failed, rejected, planning-stopped), the question asked, and a fixed list of changes that can result, with a budget rule for additions.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the post-mortem step the doc would not say what changes after a failure; the reader would find no outcome list.

demonstrations.method: For each of the six figures, find the citation or estimate label next to it; re-measure the ones the snapshot allows.
demonstrations.observes: gh.rs 5,276, produce_and_verify 724, decision log 3,231, 7 retries, planning stops and 1997 of 2000 each have a source (file, system-facts budget line, or 'stated by the request'). Figures needing records/ are labeled not measured here.
demonstrations.fails_without: An uncited figure is a finding.

demonstrations.method: Read the mapping and relations section against hestia.md section 8, requirements-map.md, BRIEF.md line 597, and a grep showing no doc names the introspector, requirements engineer, 5p65 or zc0v.
demonstrations.observes: The doc states Hermes with Hestia is confirmed with a reason, lists each of the five relations, and marks the code-health check, Jev checks, introspector and requirements engineer as not present in the snapshot (request-only). hestia.md gains a cross-reference line.
demonstrations.fails_without: Assuming those exist would show as a claim without a source file.

demonstrations.method: Read measures, cadence, budget and restructuring-queue sections and recompute one stated number (e.g. 1997/2000 = 99.85%) to confirm it is checkable.
demonstrations.observes: The doc lists what is measured, the cadence (per job post-mortem, weekly measure, per-drain budget check; estimates labeled), the 95% budget rule, and the queue cap with the filing rule; each rule has a number a reader can test.
demonstrations.fails_without: A rule without a number or cadence fails the outside-reader check.

demonstrations.method: Compare the new decisions.md entry's headings with D129's (Status, Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost, Provenance); read the build plan's acceptance bullets for behavior wording.
demonstrations.observes: A D130 entry marked proposed follows D129's format; the build plan jobs each have bullets that name a failing case before the passing case.
demonstrations.fails_without: A bullet that only says a file exists is rejected on reading.

demonstrations.method: Check the diff touches only the four doc files and CHANGELOG has the new line under Unreleased.
demonstrations.observes: Changed paths are docs/design/context-engineer.md, docs/decisions.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/design/hestia.md; no .rs, athena.toml or defaults.toml. Then cargo test --locked passes (docs checks such as the boundary scan and budget test still hold).
demonstrations.fails_without: A code or config path in the stat fails the criterion; the boundary scan test fails if banned words or email-like text are added.

open_questions: Whether the code-health check (5p65) and Jev checks (zc0v) have landed after the base commit: the snapshot has no doc for them, so the design states interface assumptions only.

The 7 lost-verifier-findings retries, the planning-stop counts and the 3,231-line figure come from the request or records/, which the snapshot lacks; the base decisions.md is already longer than 3,231 lines.
Whether the thresholds (for example file over 800 lines, function over 100 lines) fit Athena's code; they are estimates until the first measurement job.
How the 'mechanism' scan for banned words treats the role name Hermes; the producer should run the policy test.
